source_name: Hospodářská komora ČR — Česká legislativa (připomínkování)
why_relevant: The Chamber of Commerce is a formal připomínkové místo and aggregates business-side comments on draft legislation, including financial-sector drafts routed through member associations. Aggregator route into association positions when the association itself publishes nothing.

source_name: ČNB — Czech and selected foreign associations working on financial market (directory)
why_relevant: The supervisor's own curated list of the financial-market associations it recognises, with their URLs (ČBA, ADZ credit unions, ČAP, AKAT, ČASF, APS ČR pension funds, actuaries, brokers). Authoritative way to bound the association universe for this cell and to catch bodies the seed queries missed. A cs mirror exists under /cs/.

source_name: Česká kryptoměnová asociace (ČKMA)
why_relevant: Crypto-sector association that publicly claims a role in shaping the CZ law implementing MiCA and the crypto tax time/value test. Adjacent to but overlapping the payments perimeter (CASP licensing now supervised by ČNB); a cell actor the seed list did not name.

source_name: LobbyFacts / EU Transparency Register entry — Česká bankovní asociace
source_subtype: transparency register mirror / structured advocacy data
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: EU Transparency Register data on ČBA's declared EU-level advocacy — lobbying spend, staff, declared legislative dossiers of interest and meetings with the Commission. Independent, structured evidence of which regulatory files the association actually prioritises, without relying on its own publications.

source_name: EBA consultation response repository — Czech Banking Association submissions
why_relevant: ČBA files responses to EBA consultation papers, published verbatim as PDFs on the EBA site (an example ČBA response PDF and a general-remarks upload were both observed in search results). These are the association's fully-argued positions on prudential/payments rules, dated, in English — often more detailed than anything on cbaonline.cz.

source_name: Deloitte Česká republika — Regulatorní novinky (financial services regulatory newsletter)
why_relevant: Recurring Czech-language digest of ESMA/EBA/EIOPA/ECB/FSB and Czech regulatory developments aimed at banks, payment and investment firms; Deloitte's most explicitly periodic regulatory-change tracker for CZ financial services and a fast secondary layer restating EU obligations with local dates.

source_name: Deloitte Legal ČR — Regulace (financial-market regulatory advisory hub)
why_relevant: Deloitte Legal's Czech regulatory practice page; entry point to client alerts on licensing, payment services, AML and DORA readiness written for Czech regulated entities.

source_name: Deloitte ČR/SK — Novinky ze světa financí (financial services advisory publications)
why_relevant: Consolidated CZ/SK financial-services publication index on Deloitte's new domain; likely the surviving home of the regulatory newsletter series after the domain migration.

source_name: EY Česká republika — Výběr regulatorních novinek (quarterly regulatory roundup)
why_relevant: Explicitly quarterly, dated Czech-language regulatory roundup for financial services (co-published with the trade magazine Bankovnictví). Consistently names EU packages and their Czech application dates — the single most deadline-oriented Big Four series found in this cell.

source_name: KPMG Česká republika — Bankovnictví (industry insights)
why_relevant: KPMG CZ banking-sector hub publishing studies and regulatory commentary (Basel, IFRS provisioning, ESG, DORA); the Czech-language entry point to KPMG's regulatory alerts for banks.

source_name: PwC Legal EU RegCORE — Client Alerts (payments framework)
why_relevant: PwC Legal's EU RegCORE issues dated PDF client alerts on PSD3/PSR and the EU payments framework; EU-level but directly consumed by Czech payment institutions and often the earliest plain statement of trigger dates. Cross-border, not CZ-authored — use as a timeline benchmark against CZ-firm alerts.

source_name: Schönherr (Praha) — monthly 'Novinky z české a evropské regulace finančních institucí' on epravo.cz
why_relevant: Verified monthly law-firm series (authored by Schönherr's Prague office, published via epravo.cz) covering Czech AND EU financial-institution regulation with concrete dates — e.g. the January 2026 edition names 30 March 2026 for Eurosystem DLT collateral and 2026 Listing Act steps. Longest-running deadline-bearing adviser series found in this cell; runs back to at least 2021.

source_name: epravo.cz — Finanční právo section (law-firm alert aggregator)
why_relevant: The de-facto Czech clearing house where nearly every domestic law firm publishes its financial-regulation client alerts. Best single pointer for discovering new adviser actors and for catching PSD3/PSR/DORA explainer articles across firms.

source_name: HAVEL & PARTNERS — Publikace a newslettery
why_relevant: Largest Czech-Slovak firm; dedicated newsletter/publication category plus a banking-and-finance and a FinTech practice. Their alerts are the widest-circulated domestic legal updates and typically state Czech transposition dates plainly.

source_name: HAVEL & PARTNERS — H&P magazín / blog
why_relevant: Periodical magazine edition of the firm's updates plus a separate blog domain; captures longer-form regulatory readiness pieces that do not appear in the short alert stream.

source_name: PRK Partners — Banking & Finance practice / insights
why_relevant: Named target firm in this cell; long-standing Czech banking & finance practice publishing client alerts in cs and en. Entry point for their regulatory update stream.

source_name: Kinstellar — News and Insights (CEE incl. Prague)
why_relevant: CEE firm with a Prague office covering financial-services regulatory work; publishes English client insights that often cover multiple CEE jurisdictions in one piece, useful for CZ-vs-region comparison of implementation timing.

source_name: A&O Shearman — Czech Republic coverage page (Prague office publications)
why_relevant: Named target firm; Prague office (est. 1992) advising Czech banks and investment firms on MiFID, CRD/CRR, BRRD, PSD, MiCA, AMLD. Their global regulatory publications are authoritative on EU timing; CZ-specific alerts are the item to hunt from this entry page.

source_name: CMS Czech Republic — Legal updates (Banking & Finance)
why_relevant: CMS Prague publishes dated Czech legal updates including financial-market supervision changes (e.g. an update on integrating Czech financial-market regulators). Structured, indexable, and jurisdiction-tagged — easy to collect.

source_name: ARROWS advokátní kancelář — Bankovnictví, pojišťovnictví & fintech updates
why_relevant: Mid-market Czech firm publishing frequent, very practical cs-language alerts on ČNB reporting duties, licensing of foreign entities, payment-directive compliance and ČNB warnings — operational obligation detail rarely present in Big Four material.

source_name: ROWAN LEGAL — Novinky z právního světa (Banking & Finance)
why_relevant: Czech firm with a banking/finance and strong ICT-regulatory practice; relevant for DORA/NIS2 crossover obligations affecting Czech financial institutions and their ICT suppliers. Bilingual cs/en site.

source_name: Glatzová & Co. — Právní akademie: Nařízení DORA
why_relevant: Independent Prague firm running a structured 'legal academy' explainer format on DORA — a readiness/training artefact that typically lays out obligations against dates in Czech, i.e. exactly the practical-trigger-date material this cell targets.

source_name: PIERSTONE — DORA: Povinnosti a implementace (client briefing PDF)
why_relevant: Prague technology-law boutique; a downloadable cs-language DORA obligations-and-implementation briefing — a concrete example of the deadline-tracker artefact this cell exists to find, and a marker that Pierstone publishes such PDFs regularly.

source_name: SCHEJBAL & PARTNERS — DORA impact analysis / documentation service pages
why_relevant: Service-offer pages rather than alerts, but they reveal in Czech which DORA obligations Czech firms are actually buying help with (documentation sets, impact analysis) — an indirect demand signal for compliance-driven spend.

source_name: AK Duffková — Nařízení DORA explainer
why_relevant: Small-practice cs explainer; low authority individually but useful as a breadth indicator of how widely DORA obligations have diffused into the Czech adviser market, and occasionally restates dates clearly.

source_name: DUBA LEGAL — Pojišťovací a bankovní právo
why_relevant: Czech boutique covering banking/insurance and payment-transaction law; minor actor, listed for actor-map completeness and occasional payment-services commentary.
